scope: Fresh review of the concrete, unpublished GitHub-native profile application: static avatar/header, profile name/bio, readable README, three public project links and pins. Future website continuity is assessed only as a written contract. Prior mascot/motion scores are not reused as profile approval.
sourceVerification: All nine files listed in review-source-v1.json matched their SHA256 values at independent inspection.

skillsReviewed.catalogContinuity: All 17 installed Emil summaries were inspected earlier in this conversation; the prior intake remains recorded. Reuse is not claimed as new full reading.
skillsReviewed.practicalApplication: Use design-taste for plain grounded copy, real work, coherent existing identity and actual rendering; use Emil guidance for useful defaults, readable hierarchy and restraint. Mobile/native and stress-review guidance keep 320px/scroll evidence distinct from hardware or spoken-output testing. No custom UI or motion was manufactured for this static host.

workflowChanges: Review the profile in GitHub's actual native reading order, including the bio before the README and pins after it; assess repetition across those surfaces rather than treating each paragraph as an isolated component.
Use real wheel-scrolled viewport images for mobile reading claims. Ignore full-page sticky-navigation artifacts rather than diagnosing them as authored layout defects.

Audit one clear human-readable project name and purpose per public link, then inspect the pin names as the repeat-visit route. Preserve native text as the functional explanation; tiny artwork is a recognition cue.

Separate evidence of a locally rendered draft from published account state, live image delivery and audience behavior. Score the current static application; leave future website interactions unscored.

Carry verified public names, descriptions and author identity into website stories, but require new rendered and behavioral evidence at that milestone. An agreed continuity contract is not website approval.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Taste-skill commercial screen recipes, custom fonts/CSS, full-screen sections, hover layer, shaders and compulsory product renders
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: GitHub owns the layout, typography and native controls; a profile README is an introduction inside that host, not a commercial landing page. Applying these recipes would either be unsupported or reduce reading usefulness.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Taste-skill headless page-builder/checker workflow and starter asset/reference setup
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: This is a read-only review of an existing native GitHub preview, not construction of a new page. Root owns browser capture. No checker execution or custom page pass is claimed.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Motion timings, interruption checks or audio requirements carried over from character studies
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: This application deliberately uses static silent PNG artwork. No meaning or navigation requires animation, sound or a mascot interaction, so nonexistent motion/audio is neither scored nor demanded.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Mobile-native app-shell viewport/overscroll fixes or break-ui fixture injection
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: GitHub controls the shell; review supported Markdown content and recorded viewport rendering. Do not propose global scrolling/zoom changes, fake controls or arbitrary fixtures in a profile README.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Mandatory first-screen transaction or visible heyNag.com CTA
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: The profile is a personal introduction with three public work destinations. An unfinished website would be a dead destination; omission is appropriate until useful live content exists.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Prior specialist approval or a target nine substitutes for fresh evidence
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: This is a new application with its own score and deductions. Neither prior mascot consensus nor a written future website plan proves this profile's audience outcomes.

scoreMeaning: Out of 10 for the current static GitHub draft's discoverability, reading comfort and practical repeat-visit routes. Strong, clear and restrained within the native host. Minor copy repetition and limited evidence of actual visitor navigation keep the judgment bounded. The future website and audience recognition are not included in this number.

strengths.finding: Clear personal attribution precedes the character story.
strengths.evidence: The 320px top captures show Nagarjuna Boddu and heyNag beside the small avatar; desktop combines the same identity with Hey, I'm Nag. The full name remains readable without being embedded solely in artwork.
strengths.meaning: The moth supports the maker identity instead of requiring visitors to infer who owns the work.

strengths.finding: Public work has simple, direct routes.
strengths.evidence: README uses bold native text links for Charms, Grok Bot and eva.md with a concrete purpose after each; the scrolled pin capture gives the same three repositories a predictable later route. render-checks.json records the same three heyNag URLs in both themes at five widths.
strengths.meaning: A reader can choose by purpose on the first visit and use the stable names/cards on return. This is an affordance judgment, not an observed task result.

strengths.finding: Narrow reading remains comfortable and functional.
strengths.evidence: Actual 320px scrolled light/dark views wrap the descriptions without clipped text, dense side-by-side columns or hidden project names. The recorded document width equals viewport width from 320 to 1440px.
strengths.meaning: The work is native selectable text; neither tiny hand gestures nor raster text carries essential project meaning.

strengths.finding: Static/silent treatment respects reading and repeat visits.
strengths.evidence: README uses paired header PNGs with one concise fallback image description; the universal day avatar remains recognizable in the inspected light and dark contexts. No autoplay, animated badge wall or sound competes with project text.
strengths.meaning: The current profile has no motion gate and does not spend visitor attention on repeated performance.

strengths.finding: The scope of public proof is honest.
strengths.evidence: README says most work is private and presents only three public projects; profile.json omits the unfinished website destination, and neither file exposes private project names or links.
strengths.meaning: Visitors receive useful available routes without being sent to a placeholder or being shown unsupported claims.

deductions.confidence: high for repetition, moderate for its visitor cost
deductions.finding: The bio and README opening repeat software/systems, curious experiments, useful tools and care about how they feel. At 320px the native profile stack already creates distance before the work; repeating the same framing adds reading without much new information. This is a controllable copy cost, not a defect in GitHub's native chrome.
deductions.improvementCriterion: If refining the introduction, let the bio state the broad practice and let the README add one new grounded detail or reach the public work sooner. Preserve the honest private-work note and do not invent credentials or outcomes.

deductions.finding: Each project explains its concrete function well, then adds an expressive second sentence. The warmth fits Nag, but the accumulated extra lines make the three-link scan longer on a narrow screen. Charms' A few extra ways to look closely adds the least decision-useful information.
deductions.improvementCriterion: Keep warmth selectively rather than adding a coda to every entry; check that a reader can distinguish all three projects from the first sentence alone. No need to rewrite merely to hit a word count.

deductions.kind: unmeasured navigation outcome, not a demonstrated failure
deductions.finding: The local preview establishes visual wrapping, selected assets and intended link targets. It does not establish actual newcomer project selection, delayed return efficiency, screen-reader speech, physical-device use or the published account state.
deductions.improvementCriterion: Keep those claims unmade now. When the application is actually applied, check native links and image delivery in the final context; use a short observed find-a-project/revisit task if a stronger discovery claim is needed.

recommendations: Accept this as a coherent prepared local profile draft with minor copy opportunities; no concrete blocking interaction issue was found.
Preserve the three public text routes, static paired headers, universal day avatar and omitted unfinished-site link. Avoid custom pseudo-controls or animated artwork for this host.
Optionally reduce duplicated introductory wording and keep only the most useful project codas; retain personality through specific language rather than extra interface elements.
For the future site, keep useful work visible before any mascot action and retain direct source links. Review that actual implementation separately.

continuityAssessment.currentBridge: The same heyNag wordmark/moth, Nag attribution, public project names and warm plain voice form a concrete asset-and-content bridge. A larger future site can preserve these without copying GitHub's layout.
continuityAssessment.supportedPlan: continuity.json assigns the website a useful expansion: what was made, why, decisions and results, with source links and static/reduced-motion access. No mascot gate or automatic redirect is planned; these are sound stated constraints.
continuityAssessment.importantQualification: The recognition sentence about establishing shared identity immediately is a design intention, not an observed audience result. The future website is not built, and its first-visit or return-use experience cannot receive a quality score from this profile preview.
continuityAssessment.privateWorkBoundary: Private case studies remain contingent on owner-cleared material. The current public draft discloses no private project detail; future richness must not override that boundary.

unscoredOutcomes: Human recognition that avatar, header and future website belong to the same maker
Unfamiliar-visitor attribution, emotional attachment, preference or delayed recall
Actual first-visit project selection and repeat-visit efficiency
Future website layout, controls, performance, reduced-motion behavior or conversion
Published GitHub account fields, final asset delivery and live links
independence: No new partner review was read before this file was saved. No browser actions, source edits or publication were performed.
findingsTableMarkdown:
| Before | After / recommendation | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bio and README repeat the same broad practice statement. | Let each add different grounded information when refining copy. | Reduce repeated reading before the public work. |
| Three functional project descriptions each add a warm second sentence. | Keep codas selectively where they help identification or voice. | Preserve warmth without making every narrow-screen entry longer. |
| Future recognition is stated as immediate. | Treat it as a design intention until observed. | A coherent asset bridge is not proof of audience recognition. |
